questions.question: The process of conversion of ice into water vapour is known as-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sublimation**__.

__
 
• **Sublimation** is the conversion of the **solid into the gaseous phase of matter**, with **no intermediate liquid stage**.
 
• The opposite of sublimation is** "deposition"**, where **water vapor changes directly into the ice**—such as **snowflakes and frost**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 Condensation
 
 
 
• It is the process by which water vapor in the air is changed into liquid water.
 
• It is crucial to the water cycle because it is responsible for the formation of clouds.
 
• Condensation is the opposite of evaporation.
 
 
 
 

 Evaporation
 
 
 
• It is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor.
 
• The oceans, seas, lakes, and rivers provide nearly 90% of the moisture in the atmosphere via evaporation
 
 
 
 

 Evapotranspiration
 
 
 
• It is the sum of evaporation from the land surface plus transpiration from plants.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about compounds ?

options.text: The constituents can be separated only by chemical or electrochemical reactions.
The composition of each new substance is always ﬁxed.
Elements react to form new compounds.

questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is __**Compounds have a variable composition**__.

__
 
• Compounds have a **fixed composition** throughout the mass, Hence** Option 2 is Not true.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Properties of Compound**

 
 
• A compound is a substance made up of two or more elements chemically combined in a **fixed proportion by mass**.
 
• A compound **cannot **be separated into its constituents by physical processes (It can only be separated into

 its constituents by chemical processes).
 
• The properties of a compound are entirely different from those of its constituents.
 
• Energy (in the form of heat, light, etc.) is usually given out or absorbed during the preparation of a compound.
 
• The composition of a compound is fixed, the constituents are present in a fixed proportion by mass.
 
• A compound has a definite formula.
 
• A compound has a fixed melting point, boiling point.

questions.question: What is the most abundant state of matter in the universe?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma:**__

 __
 
• It is the **fourth state of matter.**
 
• The other three states are **Solid, Liquid, Gas.**
 
• A plasma is a gas that has been** energized to the point that some of the electrons break free from, but travel with, their nucleus.**
 
• It’s the **most abundant state of matter** in the universe,
 
• But plasma **can’t exist** for long under** normal terrestrial conditions.**
 
• Plasma is nothing but **ionized gas**. 
 
• Example: **Stars are the condensed form of plasma at very high temperature. The sun, like most stars, is a great big ball of plasma**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solid__: ** 

 __
 
• It is **one of the three basic states** of matter. 
 
• A solid forms from liquid or gas because t**he energy of atoms decreases when the atoms take up a relatively ordered, three-dimensional structure.**
 
• **Intermolecular attraction is more in solid.**
 
• Example:** Rock, Metal **etc
 
 
 
• **​Liquid__:**
 __
 
• An **intermediate state** between gas and crystalline solid.
 
• The most obvious physical properties of a liquid are** its retention of volume and its conformation to the shape of its container**
 
• The **Intermolecular attraction **of liquid is lesser than solid.
 
• The Kinetic energy of liquid molecules **is greater than that of solid.**
 
• Example: **Water** 
 
 
 
• **​Gas**__**:**
 
 
• **State with distinctly different properties from the liquid and solid states.**
 
• The remarkable feature of gases is that they appear to have **no structure at all. **
 
• Gases will completely fill **any closed container**; their properties depend on the **volume of a container** but not on its shape.
 
• Gaseous molecules have **greater kinetic energy** than any other states.
 
• For gas, Intermolecular attraction is** zero.**
 
• Example: **Hydrogen, Oxygen**

questions.question: Which of the following definitions of latent heat of fusion is correct?

options.text: The amount of heat energy that is required to change 1 kg of a solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is known as the latent heat of fusion.
The amount of heat energy that is required to change 10 kg of a solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is known as the latent heat of fusion
The amount of heat energy that is required to change 1 g of a gas into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is known as the latent heat of fusion.
The amount of heat energy that is required to change any amount of a solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is known as the latent heat of fusion.

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Types of heat

 
• Sensible heat and
 
• Latent heat

Latent heat**:** The heat gained or given by the substance during a change of state (from solid to liquid to gas) is called latent heat or hidden heat. The heat absorbed or given off does not cause and temperature change in the substance.

Types of latent heat:

 
• Latent heat of **fusion** of solid
 
• Latent heat of vaporization of solid.

1. Latent heat of fusion of solid

 
• The amount of heat required per unit mass of a substance at the melting point to convert it from the solid to the liquid state is called the latent heat of fusion of solid.
 
• Its unit is cal/gram.
 
• Example: Latent heat of fusion of ice
 
• The amount of heat required to convert per unit mass of the ice into the water at 0°C temperature is called the latent heat of fusion of ice.

​OR

 
• **The amount of heat energy that is required to change 1 kg of a solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point is known as the latent heat of fusion.**
 
• Latent heat of fusion of ice (L) = 80 cal/gram

2. Latent heat of vaporization of liquid

 
• The amount of heat required to vaporize a unit mass of liquid at its boiling point is called the latent heat of vapourization.
 
• Example: Latent heat of vaporization of water or latent heat of steam
 
• The amount of heat required to convert into the steam of a unit mass of water at its boiling point (100°C) is called the latent heat of vaporization of water or latent heat of steam.
 
• Latent heat of steam(L) = 540 cal/gram

questions.question: Which of the following states of matter is formed by cooling a gas of extremely low density, about one-hundred-thousandth the density of normal air, to super low temperatures?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

States of Matter: There are five states of matter.

 
• Solid
 
• Liquid
 
• Gas
 
• Plasma
 
• Bose-Eienstein Condensate(BEC)

Bose-Einstein Condensate(BEC): 

__
 
• Gases at extremely **low density are cooled to extremely low-temperature** therefore, atoms are unable to move at all and collapsed into a single quantum state. As atoms become indistinguishable they behave as a super-atom. They are super-fluids and super-conductors. Example: Helium below temperature 2.17 K.

Plasma state:

It is a mixture of free electrons and ions.

 
• The state is consists of super excited and super energetic particles that are present in form of ionized gases.
 
• Plasma is made by heating a gas to a very high temperature so that gas molecules lose all their electrons.
 
• It does not have a definite shape and volume.
 
• Example: This state is mostly observed in stars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51f00d9500a2f28bf79a82b11029fb6f4171227c0ff2491c69bcef6a46450e02.png] 

The given image shows plasma shooted from the sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solid: **Particles of matter are bounded very tightly so that it has very low kinetic energy (almost negligible) that's why it has a definite shape and volume and cannot be compressed. Example: Iron sheet, aluminium foil.
 
• **Liquid:** Particles of matter are bounded loosely so that it has low kinetic energy. The particles can move freely and randomly throughout liquid but do not break the boundaries. It has a definite volume and cannot be compressed. Example: milk, water. 
 
• **Gas: **particles are not bounded so that it has high kinetic energy. The particles can move freely and randomly anywhere. It does not have a definite shape and volume. It is highly compressible. Example: Water vapour, oxygen, hydrogen.

questions.question:
What is called conversion from a liquid state to a gaseous state?

A. Oxidization

B. Sublimation

C. Evaporation

D. Condensation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is the process by which **water changes** from a **liquid to a gas** or **vapor**. Evaporation is the primary pathway that water moves from the liquid state back into the water cycle as atmospheric water vapor.
 
• The oceans, seas, lakes, and rivers provide **nearly 90 percent** of the moisture in the **atmosphere via evaporation**, with the remaining 10 percent being contributed by plant transpiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sublimation** is the conversion between the solid and the gaseous phases of matter, with no intermediate liquid stage. an example of sublimation is naphthalene, dry ice.
 
• **Condensation** is the process by which water vapor in the **air is changed into liquid water**. Condensation is crucial to the water cycle because it is responsible for the formation of clouds. **Condensation is the opposite of evaporation.**

questions.question: Solids can be classified as ______ on the basis of the nature of order present in the arrangement of their constituent particles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**crystalline or amorphous**__.

__
 
• Solids can be classified as **crystalline or amorphous** based on the nature of order present in the **arrangement of their constituent particles**.
 
• A **crystalline solid** usually consists of a large number of small crystals, each of them having a definite characteristic geometrical shape.
 
 
• In a crystal, the **arrangement of constituent particles** (atoms, molecules, or ions) is **ordered**.
 
• It has **long-range** order which means that there is a **regular pattern** of arrangement of particles that repeats itself periodically over the entire crystal.
 
• **Sodium chloride** and **quartz** are typical examples of crystalline solids.
 
 
 
• An **amorphous solid** consists of particles of **irregular shape**.
 
 
• The arrangement of constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) in such a solid has only **short-range order**.
 
• Such portions are **scattered** and in between the arrangement is **disordered**.
 
• **Quartz is a form of SiO₂ (silica)**. It has tetrahedral SiO₄ (silicate) units which are orderly arranged in crystalline quartz. When SiO2 is melted and the melt is cooled, it forms **amorphous quartz glass**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The distinction between Crystalline and Amorphous Solids:
 
 
 

 **Property**
 **Crystalline Solid**
 **Amorphous Solid**
 
 

 Shape
 The definite characteristic geometrical shape.
 Irregular shape.
 
 

 Melting point
 Melt at a sharp and characteristic temperature.
 Gradually soften over a range of temperatures.
 
 

 Anisotropy
 Anisotropic in nature.
 Isotropic in nature.
 
 

 Nature
 True solids.
 Pseudo solids or supercooled liquids.
